statement: The table shows the results of a survey that asked $100$ students in grades 9 and 10 which lunch option they prefer. $$\begin{array}{l|c|c|c} & \text{Pizza} & \text{Salad} & \text{Total} \\ \hline \text{Grade 9} & 34 & 16 & 50 \\ \text{Grade 10} & 27 & 23 & 50 \\ \hline \text{Total} & 61 & 39 & 100 \end{array}$$ If one of the students who prefer salad is chosen at random, what is the probability that the student is in grade 10?

choices.misconception: I divided the 23 grade 10 students who prefer salad by all 100 students instead of by only the 39 who prefer salad.
I found the probability that a random student prefers salad and ignored the grade.
I divided by the 50 grade 10 students, which gives the chance that a grade 10 student prefers salad, the reverse of the question.

hints: The student is chosen only from the students who prefer salad. How many students is that?
Use the Salad column only: the denominator is the salad total, and the numerator is the grade 10 entry in that column.
There are $39$ students who prefer salad, and $23$ of them are in grade 10.

solutions.reliable: The student is chosen from the $39$ students who prefer salad, so the sample space has $39$ equally likely students. Of these, $23$ are in grade 10. The probability is $\dfrac{23}{39}$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
